result: There was a known bug in `ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory` involving deserialization of a JSON `null` into a field whose declared Java type was a primitive (e.g. `int`, `boolean`). Because primitives cannot hold `null`, the reflective field-setting code let the null value propagate into an unboxing/assignment step, surfacing as an uninformative `NullPointerException` rather than a clear Gson-level error. The fix changed the field-reading logic in that class to catch this case and rethrow it as a proper `JsonSyntaxException`/`JsonParseException` identifying the offending field, so users got an actionable diagnostic instead of a bare NPE. This was distinct from Gson's handling of `null` for reference-typed fields, which was already tolerated without issue.
